title: Service design: personas, stories, journeys, blueprints and workflows
status: Proto-personas and assumed journeys, written from the owner's requests, published guidance and the portal's own safeguards. They have not been tested with users yet: research Round 1 (January to February 2027) tests them, and they will change.
intro: Amplify is designed around the people who use it. Each persona below has needs and pain points, user stories with tests that prove them, journeys through the portal, and the service blueprints, processes and workflows that sit behind every screen.

personas.context: At secondary school; uses a phone more than a laptop; may be a young carer, care-experienced, d/Deaf or disabled, or speak Welsh, Gaelic or Irish at home.
personas.goal: Find out how to make my voice heard on something I care about, safely.
needs: Plain words at a reading age of 11 to 13
Routes that fit my age and nation
To know who to talk to if I'm worried
pains: Not knowing what is safe to share
Many services are not for under 16s
personas.safety: No sign-in, no personal data, helplines first; contributions through a trusted adult under 13.

personas.context: At college, university, work or looking for work; may vote in Scottish or Welsh elections already; may be NEET.
personas.goal: Take part directly: campaign, contribute and build skills I can show employers.
needs: Ways in that fit around work or study
personas.safety: Clear rules on what GitHub makes public; ambassador and research promises.

personas.context: Has parental responsibility; may be helping a child under 13 or under 16 use services that are age-limited.
personas.goal: Support my child to speak up and keep them safe while they do.
needs: To know what the portal asks of my child
How to act on their behalf
pains: Not understanding the online safety rules
personas.safety: Age and access rules, acting on behalf, and consent for under 16s in research.

personas.context: Runs a youth club, uniformed group or youth council; works to a safeguarding policy.
personas.goal: Plan sessions that help my group be heard, and run them safely.
personas.safety: Sessions run in the group's setting under its policy; background checks for visitors.

personas.context: Teaches citizenship, PSHE, computing or careers; plans for UK Parliament Week.
personas.goal: Use trusted, curriculum-linked material with my class in under 20 minutes' preparation.
personas.safety: Neutral, sourced content; no pupil data; posts for adults to share.

personas.role: Coding or STEM club leader or mentor
personas.context: Runs a Code Club, CoderDojo or school club; wants real projects, especially for girls and young women.
personas.goal: Give my club a real open-source project with professional practice to learn from.
needs: Clear rules for under 18s on GitHub
personas.safety: No personal data on GitHub; 13+ with parental agreement; reviews before anything goes live.

personas.role: Councillor, policy maker, researcher or journalist
personas.context: Works with or reports on young people's participation; needs to cite sources.
personas.goal: Understand youth voice across the UK and represent it accurately.
needs: Sources and dates for every fact
personas.safety: Unofficial status stated everywhere; never identify a young person.

personas.role: d/Deaf or disabled young person (any age)
personas.context: Uses BSL or ISL, a screen reader, magnification, switch access or simpler language; may have a supporter.
personas.goal: Use every part of the portal and take part on equal terms.
needs: Explainers that do not rely on hover
pains: Tooltips that only work with a mouse
personas.safety: Interpreters booked first; any modality; supporters welcome.

stories.want: see the ages and the organisations at each stage of youth representation, and find my own area
stories.so: I can get involved without being told I'm too young

stories.want: know who to contact if I'm worried, wherever I am in the portal
stories.so: I can get help quickly

Safeguarding is linked from every Get involved screen

stories.want: understand words like MYP or select committee where I meet them
stories.so: I don't give up on a screen
accept: Marked terms explain themselves on hover and focus
No tooltip is ever empty

stories.want: contribute to the portal and have it recognised
stories.so: I can show what I've done
accept: Ways to help by time and skill
Recognition and badges described

stories.want: see what changed because people like me took part
stories.so: I know it's worth my time
accept: You said, we did links each finding to a change

stories.want: act on my child's behalf where a service is age-limited
stories.so: they are not shut out
accept: Age and access table by service
On-behalf guidance in plain English

stories.want: know exactly what research would ask of my child
stories.so: I can give informed consent
accept: Promise, consent and data rules published
Under 16s need a parent's consent

stories.want: a session plan I can run tonight

stories.want: find local and national groups for young people least often heard

stories.want: sourced, neutral facts for a UK Parliament Week lesson
stories.so: I can teach with confidence
accept: Launch dates sourced
Calendar and Classroom sharing on click only

stories.want: show girls in my class that STEM is for them
stories.so: more of them choose computing and engineering
accept: Facts with linked sources
Free opportunities by path, for every nation where available

stories.want: a real pipeline my club can learn DevOps on
stories.so: they practise how professionals work
accept: DevOps steps point to real files
Every check proves it catches a deliberate break

stories.want: clear rules for under 18s contributing on GitHub
stories.so: my club stays safe in public
accept: Age rules and no personal data stated
Ambassador and research forms ask no names

stories.want: cite every fact with its source and date
stories.so: my reporting or policy is accurate
accept: Every source has a provenance and check date
Overdue sources are flagged

stories.want: describe Amplify accurately
stories.so: I don't present it as an official service
accept: Approved descriptions to copy
Unofficial status in three places

stories.want: use every screen with a keyboard and screen reader
stories.so: I am not excluded

Tooltips work on focus and close with Escape

stories.want: use the portal on a small phone at large text
stories.so: I can read it the way I need

Explainer bar wraps

stories.want: take part in research in BSL or ISL
stories.so: my experience counts
accept: Interpreters booked before sessions are offered
Any modality accepted

stories.want: see what an MP and a Member of Youth Parliament actually do all day
stories.so: I can picture myself doing it
accept: The MYP, MP and peer are shown side by side
Every fact links to its source

stories.want: a sourced explainer of Parliament's week and the Order Paper
stories.so: I can run a UK Parliament Week lesson

Each part of the Order Paper explained

stages.doing: Opens Amplify on a phone
stages.opportunity: The New here tour and explainer bar

stages.doing: Checks the ages on Your route in and finds their area on the map
Hovers or taps on a term it doesn't know
Talks to a teacher about Make Your Mark or a youth council
stages.opportunity: A trusted adult helps with the next step

stages.doing: Knows where to go if something worries them
Gets the school's message about UK Parliament Week
stages.opportunity: Parents' message says no sign-in or personal data

stages.doing: Takes the Parents and carers tour
stages.opportunity: Safeguards and age rules in one place

stages.doing: Reads age and access rules for the services involved
stages.feeling: Clear what child can do alone

stages.doing: Helps the child share an idea or join research

journeys.title: Running a session with a youth group

stages.doing: Picks a session from Training
Checks inclusion and languages for the group
Runs the activity with Your route in, the local map and Issue domains

stages.doing: Picks a good first issue and edits a data file

stages.opportunity: Checks and open items in public

blueprints.title: A young person finds a route in and takes part safely

cells: Checks ages and finds their area
Drawn in code from brand rules
Stages, ages and the local map

blueprints.title: A parent acts on behalf of a child under 16

cells: Shares or acts for the child
Share links open only on click
Online safety rules tracked on What's new

blueprints.title: A contribution goes from idea to release

cells: Opens an Idea or Bug form
Sees it in the release log
Issue forms ask no personal data
Changelog drives NEW and UPD flags

cells: Compares with the service's own site

workflows.title: Build, check and release
steps: Edit data/*.json or tools/
Run tools/build_site.py: page, art and docs are generated
Run check_repo, check_site, check_sources and check_browser
Every check also proves it catches a deliberate break
workflows.yes: Find the root cause, fix it, add a check and a negative test, log the defect, and rerun
workflows.no: Push, open a pull request; the owner merges and republishes

workflows.title: Weekly upkeep
steps: Pull and run every check
Re-verify helplines first, then sources past review
Look for dated, sourced developments
Triage issues; flag any personal data to the owner
workflows.yes: Fix it first and mark the pull request safety-critical
workflows.no: Open the weekly pull request with a plain report

workflows.title: A safeguarding concern
steps: Someone posts or says something that suggests risk
Do not reply in public or repeat the details
Point to helplines on Safeguarding & support
Tell the owner straight away
workflows.yes: Call 999, then follow the setting's safeguarding procedure
workflows.no: The owner follows the safeguarding procedure and records what was done

workflows.title: Contribution triage
steps: An Idea, Bug, ambassador or contact issue arrives
Check it contains no personal data
Decide: accept, adapt, defer or decline, with a reason
Small, safe fixes are made in the weekly run
workflows.decision: Does it need the owner's decision?
workflows.yes: List it as an open item with the owner as who must act
workflows.no: Implement, check, and record it in the release log

workflows.title: Research round
steps: Recruit through trusted organisations across the quotas
Book interpreters and support before offering sessions
Run sessions with a trusted adult present or nearby
Synthesise into themes within two weeks
workflows.decision: Does a theme exclude a group?
workflows.yes: Fix that first, before anything else in the backlog
workflows.no: Play findings back to participants, then publish You said, we did
